content: It is as easy to deceive oneself without perceiving it as it is difficult to deceive others without being found out.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
